tagline: Downstream with the Ohio, from the potteries to the Mississippi.
intro: The byway starts at East Liverpool, a pottery town where Ohio, Pennsylvania and West Virginia meet, and follows the Ohio River down the whole length of the state, through Marietta, Gallipolis and Portsmouth and past the Rankin House at Ripley, a station on the Underground Railroad, to Cincinnati.

Indiana carries it on through thirteen counties to Evansville and New Harmony, where the Harmony Society built a town and sold it after ten years, and Robert Owen's utopia there lasted only a few. In Illinois the road curls around the southern tip of the state through the Shawnee National Forest. At Metropolis a 15-foot Superman stands in front of the county courthouse.

moments.title: Fly
moments.text: For more than 200 years a ferry has crossed from here to Sistersville, West Virginia, and it is the only one still running between the two states.

moments.title: Falls of the Ohio State Park
moments.text: Across from Louisville the river lays bare beds of Devonian fossils, and Lewis and Clark met here at George Rogers Clark's cabin to begin their expedition.

moments.title: Cave-in-Rock
moments.text: A 55-foot-wide cave worn into the limestone bluff, hideout in the 1790s for Samuel Mason's river bandits and, by local lore, for Frank and Jesse James.
